articleTitle: The Evaluation Method of Tarim Low-carbon and Energy-saving Technologies Integrating the Precedence Chart Method
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Electrical, Mechanical and Computer Engineering (ICEMCE)
abstract: This article systematically explores the evaluation and application of low-carbon and energy-saving technologies integrated with the Precedence Chart method. The article details the algorithm design of the Precedence Chart method and explains the evaluation process of the Precedence Chart method in combination with the evaluation case. Through actual cases, it shows the specific applications of these models in the evaluation of low-carbon and energy-saving technologies. Through evaluating and analyzing several low-carbon and energy-saving technologies in the Tarim region, excellent (or worthy of promotion), good (or average) technologies are identified and presented in the form of cases in this article. By evaluating and analyzing several lowcarbon and energy-saving technologies in the Tarim region, excellent, worthy of promotion, good, and average technologies are identified and presented in the form of cases in this article. Through the comprehensive evaluation and analysis of low-carbon and energy-saving technologies, this article not only provides specific guidance for the energy conservation work in the Tarim region but also provides a useful reference for the low-carbon development in other regions and industries. In addition, the research results of this article also help to promote the innovation and development of low-carbon and energy-saving technologies and provide strong support for the realization of green and sustainable development goals.

articleTitle: Research on the Development and application of Memristor
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Electrical, Mechanical and Computer Engineering (ICEMCE)
abstract: This paper provides an overview of memristor devices, from their theoretical conception to practical applications. The limitations of conventional Von Neumann computer architectures are first discussed. The memristor is then introduced as a potential solution, with its unique properties of remembering resistance states. The history of memristors is reviewed, from Leon Chua’s 1971 prediction to HP’s 2008 experimental realization using titanium dioxide devices. Devices physics enabling resistance switching in HP’s TiO2 memristor are explained. Applications of memristors in non-volatile memory, logic operations, and neural network computing are described, with circuit implementations. Specifically, the use of memristor crossbar arrays for efficient multiply-accumulate operations is analyzed. Future prospects focus on memristor-based in-memory computing systems to overcome the Von Neumann bottleneck. Overall, this paper aims to illustrate the significant potential of memristors to revolutionize electronics and computing.

articleTitle: New Energy Transmission Planning Method Based on Electricity and Hydrogen Synergy
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Electrical, Mechanical and Computer Engineering (ICEMCE)
abstract: With the advancement of the construction of new power systems, there has been an imbalance in the insufficient local absorption capacity of new energy in the northwest region and the shortage of new energy in the developed eastern regions. Considering the electricity and hydrogen energy needs in the eastern region, a new energy transmission scale planning model with electricity and hydrogen synergy is constructed for the long-distance and large-capacity new energy transmission scenario. Electricity transmission in the form of high-voltage direct current transmission and hydrogen transmission in the form of hydrogen blending in natural gas pipelines are adopted. With the goal of minimizing total cost and total loss, the cost and loss of the network are considered from the source end, transmission end and load end respectively, and the constraints of supply and demand, loss, capacity and time are set. The development data of the power system and hydrogen energy system in Gansu and Zhejiang regions are used as examples for simulation analysis, and the objective function is solved by the optimization algorithm to study the optimal configuration plan for new energy transmission.

articleTitle: Review of Machine Learning Algorithms for Predictive Maintenance in Industrial Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Electrical, Mechanical and Computer Engineering (ICEMCE)
abstract: Predictive maintenance (PdM) has gained increasing importance in modern industries due to its ability to anticipate equipment failures and extend asset life. By leveraging machine learning (ML) techniques, PdM systems can analyze large volumes of operational data, identify early signs of wear, and predict remaining useful life (RUL) more accurately than traditional methods. This review delves into the application of various ML algorithms in PdM, including artificial neural networks, support vector machines, clustering algorithms, and random forests. We discuss how these algorithms enhance the ability to detect anomalies, optimize maintenance schedules, and reduce unnecessary maintenance costs. Additionally, we evaluate the challenges associated with data quality, feature selection, and model interpretability in real-world PdM implementations. The paper also provides insights into future trends, such as the integration of deep learning and IoT technologies to enable real-time monitoring and dynamic maintenance strategies that can adapt to complex industrial environments. Overall, this review underscores the transformative potential of ML-driven predictive maintenance in achieving more efficient, cost-effective, and reliable industrial operations.

articleTitle: Research and application of drilling rig optimization model
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Electrical, Mechanical and Computer Engineering (ICEMCE)
abstract: The optimal selection of drilling rigs is crucial for the rational arrangement of drilling rigs in multi operation teams, the improvement of moving operation management level, and the enhancement of drilling operation quality and efficiency. At present, the optimal selection of drilling rigs only considers whether the drilling meets the needs of the drilling project and the moving distance, and cannot comprehensively and scientifically select drilling rigs, which is not conducive to the rational configuration evaluation of oilfield drilling rig operation. This article comprehensively considers key indicators such as drilling efficiency, time efficiency, moving cycle, moving cost, and moving distance, innovatively forms a pentagonal drilling rig optimization coordinate system, establishes drilling rig optimization rate, comprehensive standard deviation, drilling rig optimization comprehensive standard deviation and other indicators, and forms a drilling rig optimization model for drilling. Taking Block B as an example, the priority of Block B with three drilling rigs to be optimized calculated using the model is ${\mathrm {R}}1\gt {\mathrm {R}}2\gt {\mathrm {R}}3$.The optimal selection rate of drilling R1 is the highest, the comprehensive standard deviation is smaller, and the comprehensive index of the best and more stable drilling performance is the highest, which is 0.0058. Therefore, R1 should be selected for drilling. The drilling rig optimization model proposed in this paper provides a process reference for drilling rig optimization, quantifies various indicators, and provides a theoretical basis for new well drilling rig optimization, project company drilling rig operation plan formulation, and improving project company drilling rig management level.

articleTitle: A Fault Diagnosis Method Based on Convolutional Decomposition and Domain Adversarial Transfer Learning for Rolling Bearing under Variable Operating Conditions
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Electrical, Mechanical and Computer Engineering (ICEMCE)
abstract: This paper proposes a rolling bearing fault diagnosis method for variable operating conditions based on convolutional decomposition and domain-adversarial migration learning. Through resampling method to balance the data samples of different categories in the dataset. The convolutional layer of the neural network is used to replace the wavelet packet transform, and the time-frequency decomposition parameters are optimized with the improved inter-domain loss to improve the time-frequency decomposition capability and reduce the time-frequency decomposition difference of migration learning for signals from different operating conditions. Multi-core feature convolution method is utilized to obtain features in the time-frequency matrix with higher correlation coefficients with migration learning fault diagnosis. Utilizing the Wasserstein distance to measure the disparity in joint distribution between domains and employing multi-kernel maximum mean discrepancy (MK_MMD) to improve domain adversarial neural network (DANN) loss function structure. This approach improves the model’s ability to fit domain distributions, reduces oscillations during optimization, and consequently enhances the model’s generalization capability and fault diagnosis accuracy in the target domain. The experimental results show that the migration learning fault diagnosis accuracy of the method proposed in this paper on the CWRU dataset is improved by 9.03% on average compared with the accuracy of the comparison models such as convolutional neural network and domain adversarial neural network, which shows an obvious comprehensive advantage compared with the comparison methods.

articleTitle: Reactive Voltage Optimization Control in Modern Power Systems Based on Deep Reinforcement Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Electrical, Mechanical and Computer Engineering (ICEMCE)
abstract: The randomness and volatility of renewable energy and loads, along with the large-scale integration of power electronic devices in modern power systems, pose new challenges to the safe operation of the power grid. Reactive voltage optimization control is fundamental to ensuring the safe and stable operation of the grid. Addressing the reactive voltage control issues caused by the large-scale integration of renewable energy, this paper proposes a reactive voltage optimization control method for power grids based on deep reinforcement learning. A reactive power optimization model is established by comprehensively considering operational efficiency, economy, and safety. The Markov decision process is used to transform the reactive power optimization problem into a reinforcement learning sequential decision optimization problem, fully considering the temporal and spatial coupling characteristics of reactive voltage control equipment. The model is solved using the Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient (DDPG) algorithm. Finally, simulation analysis is conducted on an improved IEEE 33-bus system, and comparative results verify the effectiveness and reliability of the proposed method in the reactive power optimization decision-making process.

articleTitle: A New Multi-objective Optimization Algorithm Based on Decomposition with Dynamic Resource Allocation
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Electrical, Mechanical and Computer Engineering (ICEMCE)
abstract: The Dynamic Resource Allocation Multi-Objective Optimization Algorithm (MOEA/D-DRA) is a method for solving multi-objective optimization problems (MOPs). This algorithm enhances the performance of the original MOEA/D algorithm through a strategy of dynamically allocating computational resources. However, for some challenging problems, the utility function of MOEA/D-DRA may not effectively allocate resources. This paper proposes an improved MOEA/D-DRA algorithm, introducing a new utility function to more accurately reflect the difficulty of subproblems in the current population, named MOEA/D-DRA-NEF. Experimental comparisons with ten other state-of-the-art MOEA algorithms demonstrate that MOEA/D-DRA-NEF outperforms the other algorithms in terms of convergence and diversity.

articleTitle: Point Cloud Registration Method for Power Transmission Lines based on Combined Feature Points
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Electrical, Mechanical and Computer Engineering (ICEMCE)
abstract: In view of the problems that traditional point cloud registration algorithms are inefficient and prone to local optimality when processing large-scale power transmission line point cloud data, this paper proposes a point cloud registration method based on combined feature points (CFMPCR). First, the adaptive octree is used to downsample the point cloud, and then the combined feature points are extracted by combining 3D-SIFT and Alpha Shape algorithms, and the feature points are matched by FPFH. The SAC-IA algorithm is used for coarse registration, and the improved ICP algorithm is used for fine registration, that is, the iterative closest point algorithm from point to surface combined with KD-Tree for acceleration. Experimental results show that CFMPCR is significantly superior to the traditional ICP registration algorithm in both registration accuracy and efficiency. The registration accuracy is improved by about two orders of magnitude, and the registration time is reduced by 80%. The method CFMPCR proposed in this paper has good robustness and registration accuracy when processing large-scale point cloud data, and the registration effect is better than the existing algorithm.

articleTitle: Hierarchical Recognition Method for Driving Intent Based on Single-Pedal Control
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Electrical, Mechanical and Computer Engineering (ICEMCE)
abstract: The single-pedal mode control significantly impacts the driving performance, energy efficiency, and comfort of electric vehicles (EVs). As a novel integrated pedal system, changes in system characteristics and working modes demand higher requirements for optimizing human-machine characteristics. This paper starts with the unique braking logic of the single pedal and solves the complex intent recognition problem hierarchically based on the driver’s compression of functional areas. Ultimately, we propose a hierarchical active recognition model for single-pedal intent: RBF-GMM-HMM. By applying a hierarchical approach, this model addresses the complex intent recognition challenges of the single pedal. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed RBF-GMM-HMM model effectively identifies the braking intent of the single pedal, outperforming traditional methods.

articleTitle: Personnel Detection Algorithm Based on Spatiotemporal Mapping Event Frames
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Electrical, Mechanical and Computer Engineering (ICEMCE)
abstract: The personnel detection algorithms based on frame-based traditional cameras exhibit low accuracy in harsh lighting conditions or rapidly moving scenes. To address this issue, we propose a personnel detection network called YOLO-SMCA, which utilizes an event camera to capture personnel motion information based on Spatiotemporal Mapping Event Frames. By incorporating temporal information into the event mapping method to generate event frames, we overcome the limitations of traditional event representation methods, which often lead to the loss of temporal information. This enhancement significantly improves the feature representation capability of the input events. Building on this foundation, we employ the YOLOv5n neural network for personnel detection using spatiotemporal mapping event frames. Additionally, we embed the Coordinate Attention (CA) mechanism in the head of the network to enhance the model’s focus on key features during final decision-making. Through comparative and visualization experiments conducted on the PEDRo dataset, the YOLO-SMCA achieved a mean Average Precision (mAP) of 98.1%, outperforming other methods and meeting the accuracy requirements for personnel detection in complex environments.

articleTitle: Online detection method of distribution transformer loss under harmonic disturbance
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Electrical, Mechanical and Computer Engineering (ICEMCE)
abstract: To study the online calculation method of harmonic no-load loss and harmonic load loss by using the voltage and current data of the high and low sides of the distribution transformer. Firstly, the calculation method of harmonic loss is deduced by analyzing the variation of no-load loss with frequency and flux density. Then, the least square method is used to identify the fundamental wave resistance of the winding, and the winding resistance loss model under harmonic conditions was established according to the Γ-type equivalent circuit and superposition principle of the transformer. Subsequently, based on the proportional relationship between the load losses in the improved IEEE method, the online acquisition method of harmonic load loss with Dyn11 and Yyn0 connection modes is obtained. The influence of harmonic and load variation on harmonic loss is analyzed. The computation and testing outcomes demonstrate that the proposed approach is capable of accurately capturing the variation law of harmonic loss in the operating distribution transformer, based on the harmonic number and harmonic distortion rate. Increasing the load side power factor and improving the three-phase load imbalance can effectively reduce the harmonic load loss of the distribution transformer. Nonlinear load unbalance mainly causes the increase of 3rd and 5th harmonic additional loss.

articleTitle: Optimal Dispatch of Integrated Energy System Considering Dynamic Efficiency of Electrolyzer
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Electrical, Mechanical and Computer Engineering (ICEMCE)
abstract: This paper proposes a low-carbon economic dispatching model for integrated energy system to achieve efficient energy utilization, optimize the operational flexibility of P2G equipment, and further reduce the carbon emission level of integrated energy system. Firstly, a dynamic hydrogen production efficiency model of electrolyzer is established based on Faraday’s electrochemistry theory, which considers the influence of input power and aging degree on hydrogen production efficiency. Based on this electrolyzer model, the operation of a two-stage P2G system is detailed, methanation reactor and hydrogen fuel cell are added based on traditional P2G equipment, and various consumption paths of hydrogen are studied. At the same time, the adoption of ladder-type carbon trading to control carbon emissions further enhances the low-carbon and economic performance of the integrated energy system. Finally, a dispatching model is established with the goal of a minimum sum of energy purchase cost, carbon trading cost, and wind curtailment cost. After the linearization of the proposed model, Gurobi solver is used to solve it. The effectiveness of the proposed model is verified through a comparative analysis of multiple cases.

articleTitle: Impact of Vector Control on Small-signal Synchronization Stability for Virtual SG
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Electrical, Mechanical and Computer Engineering (ICEMCE)
abstract: The virtual synchronous generator (VSG) are designed to be voltage-source external characteristics that behave with positive damping in weak grids but deteriorate low-frequency oscillation in strong grids. Using the damping torque method for low-frequency oscillation analysis of SG, this paper analyzes the effect of convertor vector control on the small-signal synchronization stability for VSGs. Firstly, comparing the damping torque of the synchro with armature reactance only and the grid-forming converter with current inner loop only, the influence of the inner loops on the small-signal synchronization stability is analyzed. Secondly, considering the voltage outer loop, the damping torque of the converter with complete vector control loops is derived, and the influence of outer loop bandwidth on the small-signal synchronization stability is analyzed. The results show that the current inner loop provides a little negative damping in the low-frequency band and has less influence on the small-signal synchronization stability. The voltage outer loop provides significant positive damping in the low-frequency band, and the damping increases with the increase of bandwidth, so it has a greater influence on the small-signal synchronization stability.

articleTitle: Analysis on the operation mode of pumped storage power station and the benefits of participating in electricity market transactions
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Electrical, Mechanical and Computer Engineering (ICEMCE)
abstract: Pumped-storage power stations play an important role in the electricity market because of their flexible operation and rapid response, as well as their multiple functions such as peak shaving and valley filling, frequency and phase modulation, and emergency standby. Based on the summary of the typical operation modes of pumped-storage power stations in the world, this paper constructs the cost-benefit model of pumped-storage power stations participating in electric energy trading and auxiliary services, and uses the data of a pumped-storage power station in the Southern Power Grid for example calculation. The results show that the difference in electricity prices between peak and valley hours leads to a significant increase in income, and the income from pumped storage participating in electric energy trading in the electricity market is not as stable as the unified dispatching mode of the power grid; the income from pumped-storage power stations participating in power frequency regulation auxiliary services is lower than the compensation level under the two-part mode.

articleTitle: Research on the Mechanism of High Voltage Cable Buffer Layer Ablation Fault
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Electrical, Mechanical and Computer Engineering (ICEMCE)
abstract: In recent years, power accidents of high voltage XLPE cable caused by buffer layer ablation failure have become common. How to reduce the possibility of ablation failure effectively and deal with a series of results that endanger the stable operation of the power system has become an urgent problem in the power industry. In this paper, the distributed equivalent electric network model and equivalent circuit of high voltage cable are constructed. The load capacity of the high-voltage cable under three different operating conditions, such as normal operation, a few white spots and ablative failure, is calculated. The electric field intensity distribution under three different operating conditions is simulated by multi-physics field model, and the ablation failure mechanism of buffer layer of high voltage cable is summarized. It can be seen from the analysis of the experimental results that with the increasing running time of the cable, partial discharge will occur, causing irreversible damage to the outer shielding layer and the main insulation layer. With the continuous accumulation of insulation damage, high-voltage XLPE cable breakdown will eventually occur, seriously damaging the cable structure and endangering the stable operation of the power system.

articleTitle: Design and Simulation Analysis of Thermal Management for Cylindrical Lithium-Ion Batteries with an Immersed Liquid-Cooled Honeycomb Structure
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Electrical, Mechanical and Computer Engineering (ICEMCE)
abstract: A cooling system featuring an immersed liquid-cooled honeycomb structure was developed for cylindrical lithium-ion power batteries. COMSOL simulation software was utilized to compute the temperature distribution within battery modules housed in this cooling configuration, under a 5C discharge rate, with both ambient and coolant temperatures maintained at $25^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$. Furthermore, the impact of varying coolant flow rates on the thermal behavior of the battery modules was analyzed. The findings reveal that, even under a high discharge rate of 5C, the liquid-cooled honeycomb structure effectively regulates the temperature of the battery pack. The peak temperature recorded was $30.7^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$, with an average of $28.5^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$, and the temperature gradient restricted to $5^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$. While enhanced coolant flow leads to improved cooling, the effect of further increasing flow rates on overall cooling performance is marginal.

articleTitle: Research on Cubic Robot Self -balance System Based on Optimized PID Control
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Electrical, Mechanical and Computer Engineering (ICEMCE)
abstract: Based on optimized PID for a cubic robot slope self balancing system with edges as the fulcrum, a control method is proposed. Firstly, based on an internally integrated momentum wheel cubic robot designed independently, a dynamic model of the cubic robot on a slope was established using the Lagrange equation, proving that it is an unstable system near the equilibrium point and has controllability and observability. Secondly, a control system based on optimized PID was designed to achieve slope self-balance control of the cubic robot. Finally, the simulation and experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of the system designed in this paper.

articleTitle: Comparative analysis of energy consumption between PHEV and REEV with P1+P3 configuration
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Electrical, Mechanical and Computer Engineering (ICEMCE)
abstract: The comparison between the series-parallel plug-in hybrid vehicle (PHEV) and series-connected REEV with P1+P3 hybrid architecture in terms of comprehensive fuel consumption and electric energy consumption under different driving conditions was made in this article. Through the research of the hybrid vehicle market and the theoretical analysis of fuel consumption models for series and parallel mode, it was found that the comprehensive fuel consumption of these two types of vehicles is not absolutely better or worse, but is closely related to the driving conditions. Therefore, a virtual model is built by Matlab/Simulink, to study the performance of fuel consumption, electric power consumption and driving range of these two types of vehicles under various driving conditions. The results show that as the proportion of high-speed segments in the driving cycle decreases, the comprehensive energy consumption of REEV gradually approaches that of PHEV, and when the ratio of low-speed segment to high-speed segment is 9:1 and 10:0, the comprehensive energy consumption of REEV is better than that of PHEV. Meanwhile, compared to PHEV, REEV doesn’t have the clutch, which also has advantages in cost reduction.

articleTitle: Dark Object Detection Based on Detail Feature Enhancement and Cross-aligned Attention
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Electrical, Mechanical and Computer Engineering (ICEMCE)
abstract: Images captured in dark and low-light environments present significant challenges for feature extraction algorithms in computer vision, particularly impacting the performance of object detection tasks due to inadequate lighting and severe noise. Previous multi-level feature extraction methods aimed to enhance performance by directly fusing features from different layers but often overlooked the misalignment and degradation of cross-scale features during fusion. We hypothesize that reducing differences between cross-level features before fusion can yield stronger feature representations. In this paper, we propose a Detail Feature Enhancement Block (DFEB) and a Detail Feature Enhancement Network (DFEN) based on it, specifically designed to enhance low-texture detail features in low-light images, thereby improving the model’s ability to capture image features from the source. Additionally, we introduce a Cross-Aligned Attention-based (CAFF) multi-level feature fusion method. Specifically, we compute cross-attention between adjacent feature layers before fusion and use deformable convolutions to integrate degraded differential feature maps into the neighboring intermediate image features, eliminating differences between multi-level detail features. This ensures that subsequent feature fusion captures more comprehensive and accurate low-light image information. By combining these components, we present a new framework for dark object detection based on detail feature enhancement and cross-aligned attention. Extensive experiments on the ExDark dataset demonstrate the effectiveness of our method in enhancing feature extraction, yielding state-of-the-art results in dark object detection tasks.

articleTitle: Study on Strategies for Enhancing Urban Power Grid Resilience through Infrastructure Network Coupling with the Power System as the Core
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Electrical, Mechanical and Computer Engineering (ICEMCE)
abstract: To study the impact of coupling systems between urban infrastructures with the power system at the core on strategies for enhancing urban power grid resilience, this research proposed strategies for enhancing urban power grid resilience in the face of extreme event disruptions. These strategies focused on the coupling systems of the power system with communication systems, transportation systems, natural gas systems, petroleum systems, and water supply systems. The study analyzed the coupling relationships between the power system and other urban infrastructures. Based on the analysis of time scales and coupling relationships, it proposed measures to enhance urban power grid resilience. Additionally, it identified critical users of the urban power grid and established an urban power grid system analysis model. Finally, through differential strengthening of urban power grid users, the study formulated strategies to improve the resilience of the urban power grid. These strategies could provide valuable reference points for decision-makers in systematically enhancing the resilience of urban power grids.

articleTitle: Research on NLOS environmental ranging method based on gradient boosting tree
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Electrical, Mechanical and Computer Engineering (ICEMCE)
abstract: Indoor distance measurement plays a critical role in positioning services. The complexity of indoor environments, coupled with a limited and small sample size, results in suboptimal distance accuracy. This paper proposes a method for non-line-of-sight distance measurement based on a gradient boosting tree model, effectively addressing the issue of sample size dependency. The random hyperparameter settings of the gradient boosting tree model lead to prolonged fitting times. Additionally, the model utilizes a fixed learning rate, which limits the analysis of features in small samples. To tackle these concerns, we develop a grid optimization algorithm that identifies the best hyperparameter combinations through a hyperparameter grid search. We also implement a weighted value approach and a cosine annealing algorithm to precisely update the learning rate according to training conditions, thus maximizing the learning of small sample features. Our proposed model significantly enhances distance accuracy in non-line-of-sight environments under constraints of training sample size and variety. Comparative experiments demonstrate that our model improves distance accuracy by 63% relative to other machine learning models, with a mean square error of only 0.168m.

articleTitle: Distributed energy generation and storage collaborative control strategy based on blockchain
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Electrical, Mechanical and Computer Engineering (ICEMCE)
abstract: With the rapid development of new energy sources, issues related to transaction transparency and security in distributed energy systems have become increasingly prominent. In response, we propose a blockchain-based collaborative control strategy for distributed energy. By leveraging the trust-building capabilities of blockchain in energy transactions and introducing cross-chain mechanisms to enhance the scalability of the energy network, the secure coordination and scheduling of distributed energy resources can be achieved. Simulation experiments demonstrate that this approach effectively addresses the challenges of integrated scheduling and trust in distributed energy production and storage, while also improving resource allocation efficiency across various energy sources.

articleTitle: A study of fireworks algorithm for cold chain logistics path optimization in karst landscape
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Electrical, Mechanical and Computer Engineering (ICEMCE)
abstract: In this study, the challenges of cold chain logistics path optimization under complex terrain conditions are explored against the background of karst landscape, and the Fireworks Algorithm (FWA) is proposed and improved to enhance the efficiency and reliability of cold chain logistics path scheduling. By analyzing the operation process of cold chain logistics in Enterprise H, a mathematical model containing multi-objective optimization of transportation cost, temperature control, time constraints and terrain complexity is constructed. The improved algorithm enhances the performance in path optimization, cost control, temperature compliance and computational efficiency by introducing dynamic spark generation strategy, multi-mode search mechanism and hybrid optimization strategy. Experimental results show that the algorithm is more applicable in multi-objective optimization problems, and can reduce transportation costs and optimize logistics paths.

articleTitle: Gearbox Fault Diagnosis Based on ResNet50-MSVEA-GATv2 Model
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Electrical, Mechanical and Computer Engineering (ICEMCE)
abstract: Addressing the issue of incomplete feature extraction during the recognition of different types of fault signals in the sun gear of a planetary gearbox and the insufficiently close node relationships in the graph neural structure operations, this paper embeds a Multi-scale Vein Expansion Aggregation (MSVEA) module into the joint ResNet50-GATv2 model, which combines a ResNet50 and a GATv2. This integration is aimed at achieving accurate classification of gearbox fault signals. Specifically, first, the ResNet50 model is used to extract features from the sub-time domain graphs segmented by sliding windows, which are then used as node information in the GATv2 model. Secondly, the MSVEA model is used to retrieve multiple strongly correlated single-line graph structures and attention algorithms are employed to redistribute the weights of node relationships. Finally, experiments and data analysis are conducted, sparsity confusion matrices of predicted categories are plotted, and four evaluation metrics for test samples are calculated. The experimental results show that the ResNet50-MSVEA-GATv2 classification model proposed in this paper outperforms other experimental groups in terms of classification results, with an accuracy rate of $\mathbf{9 6. 4 5 \%}$. This provides a new approach for applying graph neural networks in the field of mechanical fault diagnosis.

articleTitle: Optimization of UAV Intrusion Detection Based on LSTM-RNN
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Electrical, Mechanical and Computer Engineering (ICEMCE)
abstract: The increasing prevalence of Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) has resulted in a rise in malicious activities targeting their networks, highlighting the critical need for effective Intrusion Detection Systems (IDS). This study introduces an innovative intrusion detection system for UAV communication that integrates Recurrent Neural Networks (RNN) and Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks, complemented by various preprocessing algorithms to improve detection capabilities. To assess the system’s performance, a benchmark dataset was created by simulating real network traffic, and challenges related to dataset imbalance were tackled using techniques such as Synthetic Minority Over-sampling Technique (SMOTE), one-hot encoding, and min-max scaling. The evaluation on the CICIDS2017 dataset revealed that the model achieved a classification accuracy of $\mathbf{9 9. 8 4 \%}$, an F1-score of $\mathbf{9 9. 8 9 \%}$, a precision of $\mathbf{9 9. 9 9 \%}$, and a recall of 99.79%. This performance significantly surpassed that of Naive Bayes and other traditional methods, showcasing enhanced accuracy and reduced false positive rates.

articleTitle: Prediction of cascading fault accident chain in wind power systems based on CRITIC combined weighting VIKOR model
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Electrical, Mechanical and Computer Engineering (ICEMCE)
abstract: As the penetration rate of wind power in the power system gradually increases, the difficulty of predicting the path of cascading faults increases. It is of great significance to accurately search for the development path of cascading faults in the power system. A method for predicting the path of cascading faults in wind power systems based on CRITIC combined weighting VIKOR model is proposed to address the difficulty of balancing the probability and consequences of cascading faults in existing research. Firstly, based on the probabilistic power flow model, uncertain factors such as wind power output fluctuations and load changes were described, which were used as the computational basis for predicting the chain of cascading failures and accidents; Then, based on the importance and operational status of the new energy power system line structure, a severity index for the chain of cascading fault accidents is proposed; Secondly, a dual layer multi-objective decision-making method based on CRITIC combined weighting VIKOR model was established to identify lower level chain fault lines, with fault probability and fault consequence severity as the upper and lower level objectives, respectively; Finally, simulation was conducted on the improved IEEE 39 node system with wind power, and the results showed that the proposed method can predict chain failures with high probability of occurrence and serious consequences, verifying the effectiveness of the proposed indicators and methods.

articleTitle: Study on Loss Characteristics of Amorphous Alloy Transformer
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Electrical, Mechanical and Computer Engineering (ICEMCE)
abstract: Amorphous alloy transformer has significant advantages in economy and energy saving, is one of the preferred energy-saving and environmentally friendly distribution transformers of the current power system. The energy saving effect is very significant when applied in industrial areas, commercial areas, places with low load factor and rural power grids. In order to provide reference for the design, production and promotion of the use of amorphous alloy transformers, this paper analyses the no-load loss and load loss mechanism of amorphous alloy transformers, and investigates the no-load loss characteristics and load loss characteristics of amorphous alloy transformers. In addition, this paper focuses on analyzing the excellence of amorphous alloy transformers in reducing no-load losses compared with conventional silicon steel sheet transformers of the same capacity and voltage level. In this paper, a SBH15-M-400/10 three-phase oil-immersed amorphous alloy transformer is taken as the research object, and the finite element simulation software is used to establish the amorphous alloy transformer model with a two-dimensional transient magnetic field and carry out finite element simulation on it. The accuracy of the finite element simulation is demonstrated by comparing it with the no-load and load losses of this transformer obtained from analytical calculations. At the same time, the no-load loss of this amorphous alloy transformer is compared with that of a conventional silicon steel sheet transformer of the same capacity and voltage level by finite element simulation. It is shown that the amorphous alloy transformer is a low no-load loss transformer.

articleTitle: Lab-SAM: SAM-based medical image enhancement algorithm for assisted diagnosis
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Electrical, Mechanical and Computer Engineering (ICEMCE)
abstract: The Segment Anything Model (SAM) is a large-scale visual model developed for universal segmentation tasks. Due to the significant semantic differences between medical images and natural images, SAM is usually unable to provide high-quality segmentation results for medical images directly. Consequently, the investigation of the potential of SAM for medical image analysis represents a significant research topic. While SAM is currently unable to accurately segment target regions in medical images, the generated segmentation masks demonstrate the preliminary identification and localization of tissues and lesions of interest to radiologists in medical images. This implies that the segmentation output of SAM still has a potential value. Therefore, a medical image enhancement algorithm based on the output of the SAM model, Lab-SAM, is proposed. This algorithm utilizes the binary mask generated by the automatic segmentation of SAM and the corresponding information to perform feature enhancement based on the principle of attention on the input image in Lab space, thereby improving the diagnostic accuracy. In order to verify the effectiveness of the algorithm, classification experiments are conducted on different types of medical image datasets using ResNet and MobileNet. The experimental results demonstrate that Lab-SAM is capable of enhancing the training data, thereby facilitating the classification model’s ability to enhance classification accuracy. This provides a viable approach and concept for the application of SAM in disease diagnosis.

articleTitle: Interface Optimization Scheme Under Semi-Implicit Delay Decoupling Method
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Electrical, Mechanical and Computer Engineering (ICEMCE)
abstract: There exist various universal forms of semi-implicit delay decoupling. The semi-implicit delay decoupling within the state space scheme possesses second-order accuracy, yet the selected state variables must be mutually independent. When employing the nodal voltage method, the synchronization requirement of the nodal voltage method contradicts the delay characteristics of the non-semi-implicit delay-coupling model. To address this issue, a semi-implicit decoupling data interface enhancement algorithm was developed. In this paper, a semi-implicit decoupling model was constructed for the VSC converter, enabling the decoupling of the ac and dc terminals. On this basis, in accordance with the characteristics of the interface circuit, an exponential analytical solution was derived, and the interface algorithm was obtained by integrating with the decoupling model. Finally, the improved algorithm proposed herein was verified through digital examples. This algorithm improves the implicit decoupling method to a certain extent.

articleTitle: A Deep Learning-Based Bearing Fault Diagnosis Model: IEMDWave-SwinTGAMNet
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Electrical, Mechanical and Computer Engineering (ICEMCE)
abstract: In the realm of mechanical equipment fault diagnosis, the identification of bearing faults using deep learning techniques has garnered significant attention. Many researchers aim to enhance the accuracy of bearing fault detection. This paper proposes an improved IEMDWave-SwinTGAMNet model, which integrates advanced signal noise reduction techniques with deep learning methodologies. The model features a low-noise time-frequency image generation method and employs a deep neural network that utilizes a fusion attention mechanism to extract both local and global features from time-frequency images. The model’s effectiveness was validated using a bearing fault dataset from Case Western Reserve University, USA. The results demonstrate that the proposed model achieves high recognition accuracy for bearing faults.

articleTitle: Research on the measurement method of the torsion angle of the blade root of the coaxial helicopter
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Electrical, Mechanical and Computer Engineering (ICEMCE)
abstract: Aiming at the problem that the traditional torsion angle calculation method does not consider the influence of non-coplanar marking points caused by blade waving during high-speed rotor rotation, which makes the measurement results have large errors, and the measurement method of pasting marking points on the blade surface is not applicable to the propeller of dual-rotor models, a coaxial dual-rotor helicopter blade torsion angle measurement method based on binocular vision is proposed. First, fix the marker point vertically under the blade, and place the binocular camera facing the hub; secondly, collect the reference image of the marker point when the blade is flattened at a low speed and the twist image of the azimuth marker point to be measured when the blade rotates at high speed, and according to the reference image The three-dimensional coordinates of the marked points are used for plane fitting; finally, the torsion image marked points are projected on the plane, and the angle between the two three-dimensional vectors in the plane is obtained as the blade twist angle.
